title: The five functions work toward the identity's goal
goal: The five functions work toward the identity's goal: Adaptation proposes, Priority answers from the budget, Identity closes a conflict, you close what Identity cannot; what is granted runs, Audit reads it against the identity, and the loop goes on until the goal holds.
lead: J1 ends with the department made and its identity stamped by Root: the goal, the rules, done when. J2 is the department's life: Adaptation proposes what to do next, Priority answers from the budget and the present work, Identity closes a conflict between them, and you close what Identity cannot. What is granted runs; Audit reads the result against the identity; the loop goes on until the goal holds. Identity speaks to you throughout: beside every step, it tells you what was made, and asks only when a rule says ask; no other function speaks to you.
ends_when: The identity's done-when holds on Audit's reading of every item, and Identity tells you the goal is reached; Adaptation stops proposing.

steps.text: The department's Identity looks at the identity Root stamped: is it good enough to start on? If not, it asks questions until it meets its own standard; then the department starts.

Adaptation senses how far the goal is and proposes the next move: back to step 2. The loop ends on one check: does the identity's done-when now hold? Audit's reading in step 7 answers it. When it holds, Identity tells you the goal is reached and Adaptation stops proposing.

edges.code_does: priority_envelope holds the run, files one escalated 'envelope' ask that names the limit, what the engine has used and what happens next, and carries the ways forward as options built by code (hold_options): add budget (never past twice where the limit started), leave out the item only this engine is for, stop; the ledger records one event per slot however often it is asked.

outcome.golden: is out of today's envelope: it has used

edges.trigger: A workflow wants to send something outside.

site.text: Built: the first time asks once (the born rule). Your ruling S-18 says no ask unless a rule says so: open.

edges.code_does: identity_gate: Publish, or any last engine whose artifact counts after a stamp (_goes_out), asks once and then not again (publish_asks_from). It does not read the rule tag. Q14 keeps this as the one default ask.

outcome.golden: Publish: go live for the first time

edges.trigger: A result fails its check.

site.text: Built: sent back, twice at most, then you are told (_send_back).

edges.code_does: _send_back returns the build to Write with the finding, twice at most; past the second Identity still tells the owner and files one ask through _blocked with the ways out (say the rule another way, leave this rule out, stop), and choosing to leave the rule out takes it off the department's rules (leave_rule_out) so the line builds again without it. While the cycle is active, before its goal is reached, the ledger records each failed run as one run.failed event; once the goal is reached (the cycle is done) j2_runtime.on_run writes nothing, so a build that fails after that is sent back and asked about, but its failed runs are not all on the ledger (BL-4b). A failed run never ends in a tell only.

outcome.golden: two rewrites did not mend it

edges.trigger: You change the goal.

site.text: Open: through Root again (a new stamp on the identity), or Identity takes your words directly.

edges.code_does: reopen_on_change: a stamped goal rule, or a stamped change to done-when, on a department whose cycle has started calls j2_runtime.reopen, which starts a new cycle at step 1 with the record kept; its first event is goal.revised, carrying the identity's revision before and after and what changed; what the old cycle asked of the owner is retired, work in flight finishes, and Identity says the old goal and the new in one line. After done a task is the Brief's and starts no cycle; a rule that is not about the goal reopens nothing.

outcome.golden: The department starts its work again from the top

sub.title: Is the identity good enough?
sub.text: Identity checks what Root stamped, asks until it meets its standard, then starts the department. Founder 2026-10-01: knowing the identity is good enough; Identity and its journeys are to define (needs to be filled).

sub.title: Deciding what to do next
sub.text: Adaptation reads the identity and makes the workflows: from the Library or its own. This is where workflows are created. Founder 2026-10-01: a template if there is one; with no template, Adaptation makes the workflow from the identity, the goal and the practices in place; that process is the focus (needs to be filled).

sub.title: The bargain
sub.text: Adaptation proposes; Priority answers grant, refuse, counter; bounded.

sub.title: Closing a conflict
sub.text: They cannot agree: Identity closes it; what it cannot settle comes to you.

sub.title: Root's check
sub.text: A granted workflow meets the standards or is sent back; registered on the record.

sub.title: Running the work
sub.text: Coordination gives one workflow its turn; it runs step by step, AI inside, code around; it files what it made; the envelope holds it.
sub.drawn: Coordination: who goes first; Priority: the envelope; one workflow's own run: not drawn yet

sub.title: Reading the result
sub.text: Audit samples, checks, judges against the identity and files a finding. Identity weighs it three ways: a missing fact only you know becomes a question to you; a wrong that needs your yes becomes an ask; anything else goes back to Adaptation as the next thing to do.

sub.title: The next move, or done
sub.text: Adaptation senses the gap and proposes again, or learns, crystallizes, grows; when done-when holds, Identity says so.

rulings.text: Coordination keeps the table and the tie; Priority prices and holds the budget, never orders.
Authority: the AI has the whole authority to make things happen unless a person says something; no ask stops a run by default; a person narrows with a rule, a Stop, a refusal.
A template may bring default engines; the department's Adaptation overlays what it needs, unless the template says explicitly that an engine has to be there.
At the start, the inside of every box is AI only; nothing deterministic lives in an inside; a box climbs the ladder to code as its rows earn it.
The box: every engine and function is a black box with a covering of code and an inside of AI; the same shape at two levels, engine and step.
A granted workflow is registered on the department's record by Root; it does not go into the Library. (The page cites S-25; its row is not in the saved ruling table.)
The Make module: three levels; a first version is always made; going down a level is the only move when not confident.
Version 1 of each function is one AI agent with .md files inside the covering; amended by A1: typed fields, no .md files.

J2 is the five functions working toward the identity's goal, designed on the recorded thesis: Adaptation and Priority work with each other; a conflict is closed by Identity, and what Identity cannot settle comes to me. Keep it simple; evolve later.

Verification as a product: a goal is a reality articulated enough that an LLM can test it; Audit uses the verification templates at workflow and work-item level. Marks owed on the four levels, the five angles, the v1 way and the three components.

quotes.text: Identity has to be stamped by the root. Once identity is good enough, then the department starts. If, at times, it happens that the identity is not good enough, then identity will ask questions of itself to reach its standards. Once it's done, how will the workflow look between these 5 functions to reach the goal of the identity? I think that is the journey.
I think the original thesis was that adaptation and priority work with each other, and if there is a conflict, then I need to resolve it somewhere. That is how we have designed it.
2 to 5 workflows, there is no limit to that.
Keep it simple for now the way you have written. We can always evolve it later on.
The high level makes sense, though all nine steps, the ninth step is not clear. The first eight steps are clear.
For now, you can just keep these eight journeys and go with this. For the detailing of these journeys, you can do it later on.
I think knowing the identity is good enough. We need to define identity and its journeys.

Deciding what to do next: first, workflow from the library template or automation from identity. Default is a template if there is one, but if there is no template, then how do we solve for it? What's the process of adaptation for doing that? I want to focus on that. There, I want to take identities and goals, and use how much logic, considering various practices, is in place. This is the shape, and other various ways to create workflows and logic will come. There, I want to go deeper into it.

backlog.smallest: A failed run is one run.failed event on the ledger whether the cycle is active or done: j2_runtime.on_run, which returns early when active() is false, also records the failed runs of a cycle that has reached its goal, and moves no state.

The organic kind (v2.306.21): Adaptation shapes the whole line from the first words, one stamp births it. The earlier rows of this journey are kept in the data file under was.

steps.text: The department's Adaptation lays its overlay on the template's engines: the ones the template marks as must-have stay; the rest it keeps, swaps for a Library engine, or replaces with one made on the spot from your answers. A code check holds the result (unique names, the first reads the Brief, each reads what one before it wrote, the must-haves present).

steps.text: The department's Identity files your words as the Brief; the first engine wakes on it. What goes outside asks you first only if a rule says so, or if the born rule about the first publish stands (your open call, J2 step 6).
Every 3 s the motor asks Coordination who goes first; one run per department per tick.
Plan is ready: a Brief version it has not run on. Its blockers run in order: no engine ask pending; Identity's gate; Priority's envelope; the chain under 12.
steps.site_code: ready, blocked: identity.wait_engine, identity.gate, priority.envelope, coord.chain

steps.text: Plan runs: read the Brief (code), propose the pages (model), fit (code), file the Site plan v1 with its check. The chat shows "Plan is working: …".
Write wakes on the Site plan: one model call per page, four side by side; Pages v1.
Check wakes on the Pages: lists the stamped rules that apply (code); reads each page against them (model, only when there are any); builds; Build v1 with its check.
Publish wakes on a checked Build but Identity's gate holds it: the first publish ask, "go live for the first time, served from <host>".
You stamp. The host stays on the record.
Publish copies the build to the served site: Live site v1. You are told "Live site v1 is live." with Open the live site; the tell reaches Root's board too.

Audit wakes on the checked Live site: samples (versions 1 to 3, then every third); the mechanical checks; the judge (facts the Brief and the department's own filings do not give); files a finding to Identity.
Identity turns the holes ("to be confirmed") into a facts question in the chat; a high-severity finding into an ask, "Audit found: … Stamp to have it put right."
Adaptation wakes on the checked Live site: senses, reads the ladder, proposes a step's move up to Priority; granted, to you as a rung ask.
